title: Bottle & Glass Inn, Dudley
geometryBasis: Native mapped pub footprint. Wide painted front with two upper sashes and two ground-front bays, original brick chimney stacks and connected wings.
sectionBasis: The exact Jack1956 Qualla photograph documents the painted pub frontage at the end of Coppice Street. The museum building sheet confirms the historic pub and its translocation. Rear roof and heights are estimated from the mapped outline and scale of the front.
limitations: The model covers the inn and its attached ranges. The village’s other independent buildings remain outside this placement.
Street elevation, window count, cream and green painted front and historic lettering follow the Qualla photo. Rear openings and small secondary ornament are representative.
